about.title: Roseville Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When someone dies because another person or company was careless, California law gives certain family members a way to hold that party accountable in civil court. In Roseville, that path often begins after a collision. Public collision records show 7 traffic deaths in the city in 2025, alongside 808 injury collisions on roads such as I-80, Pleasant Grove Boulevard, Douglas Boulevard and Cirby Way. Crashes are not the only cause, though. Falls at a business, medical errors, workplace incidents and defective products can also support a claim. Standing is limited: a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. The claim is separate from any criminal case, and it runs on its own clock: generally two years from the date of death, shorter when a public agency is involved. We handle wrongful death cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: Clarity on Who Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. We can explain where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Explained
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a city, county or state agency may be responsible. Early guidance protects that deadline.

items.title: Every Loss Accounted For
items.desc: Recoverable losses go beyond funeral and burial costs to include lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. Our team documents each one.

items.question: A criminal case was filed after my relative's death in Roseville. Do I still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, the two are separate. The Placer County District Attorney decides whether to prosecute, and that case does not pay your family for its losses. A wrongful death claim is a civil action your family controls, and it can move forward whether or not criminal charges are brought or result in a conviction.

items.question: How long do we have to act after a death in Placer County?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government entity might share responsibility, such as a claim involving a public road or vehicle, the deadline is considerably shorter and a formal claim must come first. Speaking with us early keeps those options open.

items.question: What does it cost to contact us?
items.answer: Nothing. We handle wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery for your family.
